rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
date_bounds AS (
  SELECT
    MIN(txn_date) AS min_date,
    MAX(txn_date) AS max_date
  FROM customer_transactions
),
bounds AS (
  SELECT
    strftime('%Y', date(substr(min_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(min_date,4,2) || '-01')) AS start_yr,
    CAST(strftime('%m', date(substr(min_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(min_date,4,2) || '-01')) AS INTEGER) AS start_m,
    strftime('%Y', date(substr(max_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(max_date,4,2) || '-01')) AS end_yr,
    CAST(strftime('%m', date(substr(max_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(max_date,4,2) || '-01')) AS INTEGER) AS end_m
  FROM date_bounds
),
months AS (
  -- recursive generation of months between overall min and max txn dates
  SELECT
    CAST(start_yr AS INTEGER) AS year,
    start_m AS month_num,
    date(start_yr || '-' || printf('%02d', start_m) || '-01') AS month_start,
    date(start_yr || '-' || printf('%02d', start_m) || '-01', '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end
  FROM bounds
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    CASE WHEN month_num = 12 THEN year + 1 ELSE year END,
    CASE WHEN month_num = 12 THEN 1 ELSE month_num + 1 END,
    date(year || '-' || printf('%02d', month_num) || '-01', '+1 month'),
    date(year || '-' || printf('%02d', month_num) || '-01', '+2 month', '-1 day')
  FROM months, bounds
  WHERE NOT (year = CAST(bounds.end_yr AS INTEGER) AND month_num = bounds.end_m)
),
monthly_txn AS (
  -- aggregate net txn amount per customer per month
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', date(substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-01')) AS INTEGER) AS year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', date(substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-01')) AS INTEGER) AS month_num,
    SUM(txn_amount) AS month_net
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id, year, month_num
),
customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
)
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  m.year,
  m.month_num AS month,
  m.month_end AS month_end_date,
  COALESCE(
    -- closing balance = cumulative sum of month_net up to and including this month
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(month_net),0)
     FROM monthly_txn mt
     WHERE mt.customer_id = c.customer_id
       AND (mt.year < m.year OR (mt.year = m.year AND mt.month_num <= m.month_num))
    ),
    0
  ) AS closing_balance,
  COALESCE(
    -- monthly change = month_net for this month (0 if none)
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(month_net),0)
     FROM monthly_txn mt2
     WHERE mt2.customer_id = c.customer_id
       AND mt2.year = m.year
       AND mt2.month_num = m.month_num
    ),
    0
  ) AS monthly_change,
  COALESCE(
    -- cumulative_balance same as closing_balance (kept for clarity)
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(month_net),0)
     FROM monthly_txn mt3
     WHERE mt3.customer_id = c.customer_id
       AND (mt3.year < m.year OR (mt3.year = m.year AND mt3.month_num <= m.month_num))
    ),
    0
  ) AS cumulative_balance
FROM customers c
CROSS JOIN months m
ORDER BY c.customer_id, m.year, m.month_num

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages
rows.pred_sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT '2020-01' AS ym UNION ALL SELECT '2020-02' UNION ALL SELECT '2020-03' UNION ALL SELECT '2020-04'
  UNION ALL SELECT '2020-05' UNION ALL SELECT '2020-06' UNION ALL SELECT '2020-07' UNION ALL SELECT '2020-08'
  UNION ALL SELECT '2020-09' UNION ALL SELECT '2020-10' UNION ALL SELECT '2020-11' UNION ALL SELECT '2020-12'
),
all_customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
),
cust_month_txn AS (
  -- compute month-end balance per customer per month from transactions in 2020
  SELECT
    ct.customer_id,
    substr(ct.txn_date,1,7) AS ym,
    SUM(CASE WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) 
      - SUM(CASE WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) IN ('withdrawal','withdraw') THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS month_balance
  FROM customer_transactions ct
  WHERE date(ct.txn_date) >= date('2020-01-01') AND date(ct.txn_date) < date('2021-01-01')
  GROUP BY ct.customer_id, ym
),
-- ensure every customer-month present; missing -> balance 0
customer_months AS (
  SELECT a.customer_id, m.ym
  FROM all_customers a CROSS JOIN months m
),
customer_month_balances AS (
  SELECT cm.customer_id, cm.ym,
         COALESCE(cmt.month_balance, 0) AS month_balance
  FROM customer_months cm
  LEFT JOIN cust_month_txn cmt
    ON cm.customer_id = cmt.customer_id AND cm.ym = cmt.ym
),
monthly_stats AS (
  SELECT
    ym,
    SUM(CASE WHEN month_balance > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive_customer_count,
    AVG(month_balance) AS avg_month_end_balance
  FROM customer_month_balances
  GROUP BY ym
),
max_month_row AS (
  SELECT ym AS max_month, positive_customer_count AS max_month_positive_customer_count, avg_month_end_balance AS max_month_average_month_end_balance
  FROM monthly_stats
  WHERE positive_customer_count = (SELECT MAX(positive_customer_count) FROM monthly_stats)
  ORDER BY ym ASC
  LIMIT 1
),
min_month_row AS (
  SELECT ym AS min_month, positive_customer_count AS min_month_positive_customer_count, avg_month_end_balance AS min_month_average_month_end_balance
  FROM monthly_stats
  WHERE positive_customer_count = (SELECT MIN(positive_customer_count) FROM monthly_stats)
  ORDER BY ym ASC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT
  m.max_month,
  m.max_month_positive_customer_count,
  m.max_month_average_month_end_balance,
  n.min_month,
  n.min_month_positive_customer_count,
  n.min_month_average_month_end_balance,
  (m.max_month_average_month_end_balance - n.min_month_average_month_end_balance) AS average_difference
FROM max_month_row m CROSS JOIN min_month_row n

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH monthly_nets AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(substr(txn_date,1,7) || '-01') AS month_start,
    SUM(CASE WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
             WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
             ELSE 0 END) AS monthly_net
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id, month_start
),
ordered_months AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    month_start,
    monthly_net,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start) AS rn
  FROM monthly_nets
),
closing_balances AS (
  SELECT
    m.customer_id,
    m.month_start,
    m.monthly_net,
    (SELECT SUM(m2.monthly_net)
     FROM ordered_months m2
     WHERE m2.customer_id = m.customer_id AND m2.month_start <= m.month_start) AS closing_balance,
    m.rn
  FROM ordered_months m
),
most_recent_with_prior AS (
  SELECT
    cur.customer_id,
    cur.month_start AS recent_month,
    cur.closing_balance AS recent_closing,
    prev.closing_balance AS prior_closing
  FROM closing_balances cur
  JOIN closing_balances prev
    ON cur.customer_id = prev.customer_id
   AND cur.rn = prev.rn + 1
  WHERE cur.rn = (SELECT MAX(rn) FROM ordered_months om WHERE om.customer_id = cur.customer_id)
),
growths AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    CASE
      WHEN prior_closing = 0 THEN recent_closing * 100.0
      ELSE (recent_closing - prior_closing) / CAST(prior_closing AS REAL)
    END AS growth_rate
  FROM most_recent_with_prior
)
SELECT
  100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) / COUNT(*) AS percentage_of_customers_with_growth_rate_gt_5
FROM growths

rows.question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH chunk_view_0 AS (
SELECT
  txn_date AS txn_date,
  customer_id AS customer_id,
  txn_amount AS txn_amount,
  txn_type AS txn_type
FROM customer_transactions
),
chunk_view_1 AS (
SELECT
  "market_date" AS month,
  "price" AS previous_total_balance
FROM "bitcoin_prices"
)
SELECT
  strftime('%Y-%m', date(first_day)) AS month,
  SUM(COALESCE(CASE WHEN balance_as_of_first_day < 0 THEN 0 ELSE balance_as_of_first_day END, 0)) AS previous_total_balance
FROM (
  -- compute each customer's balance as of the first day of each month present in the data
  SELECT
    cust.customer_id,
    months.first_day,
    (
      SELECT
        SUM(
          CASE
            WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount
            ELSE -ct.txn_amount
          END
        )
      FROM customer_transactions ct
      WHERE ct.customer_id = cust.customer_id
        AND date(ct.txn_date) < months.first_day
    ) AS balance_as_of_first_day
  FROM
    (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions) cust
  CROSS JOIN
    (
      -- list of first days of months present in the transactions (one per distinct month)
      SELECT DISTINCT date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(txn_date))) AS first_day
      FROM customer_transactions
    ) months
) per_cust_month
-- exclude the earliest month overall
WHERE date(first_day) > (
  SELECT MIN(date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(txn_date)))) FROM customer_transactions
)
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month ASC

rows.question: For a bank database with customer transactions, calculate each customer's daily running balance (where deposits add to the balance and other transaction types subtract). For each customer and each day, compute the 30-day rolling average balance (only after having 30 days of data, and treating negative averages as zero). Then group these daily averages by month and find each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within each month. Sum these maximum values across all customers for each month. Consider the first month of each customer's transaction history as the baseline period and exclude it from the final results, presenting monthly totals of these summed maximum 30-day average balances.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
-- normalize txn_date to ISO YYYY-MM-DD
txns AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    txn_type,
    CASE WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END AS signed_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
),
-- get full calendar per customer (one row per customer per date that has any transaction),
-- and daily net change (sum of signed amounts per day)
daily_changes AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date AS dt,
    SUM(signed_amount) AS daily_net
  FROM txns
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
),
-- determine each customer's first transaction date (used to drop their first month)
first_txn AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(dt) AS first_txn_date FROM daily_changes GROUP BY customer_id
),
-- produce running daily balance per customer by ordering dates and cumulatively summing daily_net
running_balance AS (
  SELECT
    dc.customer_id,
    dc.dt,
    -- cumulative sum of daily_net up to and including this date
    SUM(dc.daily_net) OVER (PARTITION BY dc.customer_id ORDER BY dc.dt ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS balance,
    ft.first_txn_date
  FROM daily_changes dc
  JOIN first_txn ft USING (customer_id)
),
-- compute 30-day rolling average of the balance for each customer and date
-- only when there are at least 30 days up to that date for that customer
rolling_30 AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    dt,
    -- average over last 30 days including current row; NULL if fewer than 30 rows in window
    AVG(balance) OVER (
      PARTITION BY customer_id
      ORDER BY dt
      ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS avg_30d,
    first_txn_date,
    -- count rows in the same window to check whether we have 30 days
    COUNT(balance) OVER (
      PARTITION BY customer_id
      ORDER BY dt
      ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS rows_in_window
  FROM running_balance
),
-- keep only rows where we have full 30-day history, clamp negatives to zero, and attach month
valid_30d AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    dt,
    CASE WHEN avg_30d IS NULL THEN NULL
         WHEN avg_30d < 0 THEN 0.0
         ELSE avg_30d END AS nonneg_30d_avg,
    first_txn_date,
    strftime('%Y-%m', dt) AS month
  FROM rolling_30
  WHERE rows_in_window >= 30 AND avg_30d IS NOT NULL
),
-- determine the first month rank per customer to allow excluding the customer's first month of transactions
first_months AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', first_txn_date) AS first_month
  FROM first_txn
),
-- for each customer and month (excluding their first month), find the maximum 30-day average within that month
monthly_max_per_customer AS (
  SELECT
    v.customer_id,
    v.month,
    MAX(v.nonneg_30d_avg) AS monthly_max_30d_avg
  FROM valid_30d v
  LEFT JOIN first_months f ON v.customer_id = f.customer_id
  WHERE v.month <> f.first_month
  GROUP BY v.customer_id, v.month
),
-- sum those maxima across all customers per month
monthly_totals AS (
  SELECT
    month,
    SUM(monthly_max_30d_avg) AS monthly_total_max_30day_avg_balance
  FROM monthly_max_per_customer
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT
  month,
  monthly_total_max_30day_avg_balance
FROM monthly_totals
ORDER BY month

rows.question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH chunk_view_0 AS (
SELECT
  customer_transactions.customer_id,
  customer_transactions.txn_date,
  customer_transactions.txn_amount,
  -- keep txn_type for possible balance semantics later
  customer_transactions.txn_type
FROM customer_transactions
),
chunk_view_1 AS (
SELECT
  txn_date AS txn_date,
  "index" AS "index",
  item_code,
  "qty_sold(kg)" AS qty_sold_kg,
  "unit_selling_px_rmb/kg" AS unit_selling_px_rmb_per_kg,
  "sale/return" AS sale_return,
  "discount(%)" AS discount_pct,
  day_of_week
FROM veg_txn_df
),
chunk_view_2 AS (
SELECT
  -- This chunk doesn't contain transaction or customer tables, so output minimal placeholder columns
  -- that could be used to join to transaction/customer data in later chunks.
  NULL AS month,
  NULL AS monthly_total
)
SELECT
  month,
  SUM(monthly_customer_max) AS monthly_total
FROM (
  WITH
  -- per-customer aggregated net change per txn_date
  cust_day_changes AS (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      date(txn_date) AS day,
      SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) AS day_net_change
    FROM customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id, date(txn_date)
  ),
  -- customers with their min and max dates
  cust_ranges AS (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      MIN(date(day)) AS start_date,
      MAX(date(day)) AS end_date
    FROM cust_day_changes
    GROUP BY customer_id
  ),
  -- expand calendar days per customer using recursion
  cust_calendar AS (
    SELECT customer_id, start_date AS day, end_date
    FROM cust_ranges
    UNION ALL
    SELECT cc.customer_id,
           date(cc.day, '+1 day'),
           cc.end_date
    FROM cust_calendar cc
    WHERE date(cc.day, '+1 day') <= cc.end_date
  ),
  -- attach net changes (zero if none) and compute running balance per customer by date
  cust_daily_balances AS (
    SELECT
      cc.customer_id,
      cc.day,
      COALESCE(cdc.day_net_change, 0) AS day_net_change
    FROM cust_calendar cc
    LEFT JOIN cust_day_changes cdc
      ON cdc.customer_id = cc.customer_id
     AND cdc.day = cc.day
  ),
  -- cumulative running balance per customer ordered by day
  cust_running AS (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      day,
      -- running sum of net changes up to this day
      SUM(day_net_change) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY day ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_balance
    FROM cust_daily_balances
  ),
  -- apply non-negative rule and extract month
  cust_running_nonneg AS (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      day,
      CASE WHEN running_balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE running_balance END AS daily_balance,
      strftime('%Y-%m', day) AS month
    FROM cust_running
  ),
  -- per-customer per-month maximum daily balance (only months where customer has days)
  cust_month_max AS (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      month,
      MAX(daily_balance) AS monthly_customer_max
    FROM cust_running_nonneg
    GROUP BY customer_id, month
  )
  SELECT month, monthly_customer_max
  FROM cust_month_max
)
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month ASC

rows.question: Can you provide a breakdown of how many times each product was viewed, how many times they were added to the shopping cart, and how many times they were left in the cart without being purchased? Also, give me the count of actual purchases for each product. Ensure that products with a page id in (1, 2, 12, 13) are filtered out.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH chunk_view_0 AS (
SELECT
  -- product identifier: using 'ticker' as a proxy for product id/name available in this chunk
  bitcoin_transactions.ticker AS product_id,
  -- count of page views: no explicit page views table in this chunk, include possible proxy columns for later joins
  NULL AS views_count,
  -- count of adds to cart: no explicit add-to-cart in this chunk; include txn_type and quantity for later aggregation
  SUM(CASE WHEN bitcoin_transactions.txn_type = 'ADD_TO_CART' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS added_to_cart_count,
  -- count of left-in-cart: no explicit left-in-cart flag here; include an indicator using txn_type 'LEFT_IN_CART' for later logic
  SUM(CASE WHEN bitcoin_transactions.txn_type = 'LEFT_IN_CART' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS left_in_cart_count,
  -- purchases count: count BUY transactions as purchases (proxy)
  SUM(CASE WHEN bitcoin_transactions.txn_type = 'BUY' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS purchases_count,
  -- keep keys and useful columns for joins/filters
  bitcoin_transactions.txn_id,
  bitcoin_transactions.member_id,
  bitcoin_transactions.txn_date,
  bitcoin_transactions.quantity,
  bitcoin_transactions.ticker
FROM
  bitcoin_transactions
-- Note: filtering out product page ids (1,2,12,13) cannot be applied here because no page_id column exists in this chunk.
GROUP BY
  bitcoin_transactions.ticker,
  bitcoin_transactions.txn_id,
  bitcoin_transactions.member_id,
  bitcoin_transactions.txn_date,
  bitcoin_transactions.quantity,
  bitcoin_transactions.ticker
)
SELECT
  scph.product_id AS product_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN sci.event_name = 'Page View' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS views_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN sci.event_name = 'Add to Cart' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS added_to_cart_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN sci.event_name IN ('Left in Cart','Abandoned Cart','Remove from Cart') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS left_in_cart_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN sci.event_name IN ('Purchase','Checkout','Order Complete') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS purchases_count
FROM shopping_cart_page_hierarchy scph
JOIN shopping_cart_events sce
  ON sce.page_id = scph.page_id
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier sci
  ON sci.event_type = sce.event_type
WHERE scph.page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13)
GROUP BY scph.product_id

rows.question: Please analyze our interest data from September 2018 to August 2019. For each month, calculate the average composition for each interest by dividing the composition by the index value. Identify the interest with the highest average composition value each month and report its average composition as the max index composition for that month. Compute the three-month rolling average of these monthly max index compositions. Ensure the output includes the date, the interest name, the max index composition for that month, the rolling average, and the names and max index compositions of the top interests from one month ago and two months ago.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH per_interest AS (
  SELECT
    month_year,
    interest_id,
    AVG(composition / index_value) AS avg_ratio,
    -- build a sortable month_start date like 'YYYY-MM-01'
    DATE(substr(month_year,4,4) || '-' || substr(month_year,1,2) || '-01') AS month_start
  FROM interest_metrics
  WHERE
    (
      (_year = 2018 AND _month >= 9)
      OR (_year = 2019 AND _month <= 8)
    )
    AND index_value <> 0
  GROUP BY month_year, interest_id
),
monthly_top_picks AS (
  -- for each month pick the interest(s) with the maximal avg_ratio
  SELECT
    p.month_year,
    p.month_start,
    p.interest_id,
    p.avg_ratio
  FROM per_interest p
  JOIN (
    SELECT month_year, MAX(avg_ratio) AS max_ratio
    FROM per_interest
    GROUP BY month_year
  ) m ON p.month_year = m.month_year AND p.avg_ratio = m.max_ratio
),
monthly_top AS (
  -- if multiple interests tie for max, pick the alphabetically first interest_name
  SELECT
    mt.month_start,
    mt.month_year,
    im.interest_name,
    mt.avg_ratio AS max_index_composition,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mt.month_start ORDER BY im.interest_name ASC) AS rn
  FROM monthly_top_picks mt
  JOIN interest_map im ON mt.interest_id = im.id
)
SELECT
  month_start AS date,
  interest_name,
  ROUND(max_index_composition, 10) AS max_index_composition,
  ROUND(AVG(max_index_composition) OVER (ORDER BY month_start ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 10) AS rolling_avg_3mo,
  LAG(interest_name,1) OVER (ORDER BY month_start) AS prev_month_interest_name,
  LAG(max_index_composition,1) OVER (ORDER BY month_start) AS prev_month_max_index_composition,
  LAG(interest_name,2) OVER (ORDER BY month_start) AS prev_2mo_interest_name,
  LAG(max_index_composition,2) OVER (ORDER BY month_start) AS prev_2mo_max_index_composition
FROM (
  -- take only the chosen interest per month (rn = 1)
  SELECT month_start, interest_name, max_index_composition
  FROM monthly_top
  WHERE rn = 1
) t
ORDER BY month_start

rows.question: Identify the top 10 and bottom 10 interest categories based on their highest composition values across all months. For each category, display the time(MM-YYYY), interest name, and the composition value

WITH max_composition_per_interest AS (

  GROUP BY interest_id
),
interest_with_max AS (

ORDER BY composition_value DESC
LIMIT 10

FROM interest_with_max iwm
JOIN interest_map imap
  ON iwm.interest_id = imap.id

rows.question: Analyze the annual average purchase price per Bitcoin by region, computed as the total dollar amount spent divided by the total quantity purchased each year, excluding the first year's data for each region. rows.question: Using the "bitcoin_prices" table, please calculate the daily percentage change in trading volume for each ticker from August 1 to August 10, 2021, ensuring that any volume ending in "K" or "M" is accurately converted to thousands or millions, any "-" volume is treated as zero, only non-zero volumes are used to determine the previous day's volume, and the results are ordered by ticker and date.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH parsed AS (
  SELECT
    ticker,
    -- convert market_date like '29-08-2021' to '2021-08-29' for easy comparisons
    substr(market_date, 7, 4) || '-' || substr(market_date, 4, 2) || '-' || substr(market_date, 1, 2) AS iso_date,
    -- normalize volume: '-' -> 0, strip commas/spaces, handle K/M (case-insensitive)
    CASE
      WHEN trim(volume) = '-' OR volume IS NULL THEN 0.0
      ELSE
        (
          -- remove any commas and spaces
          CASE
            WHEN upper(trim(volume)) LIKE '%M' THEN
              CAST(replace(replace(substr(trim(volume), 1, length(trim(volume)) - 1), ',', ''), ' ', '') AS REAL) * 1000000.0
            WHEN upper(trim(volume)) LIKE '%K' THEN
              CAST(replace(replace(substr(trim(volume), 1, length(trim(volume)) - 1), ',', ''), ' ', '') AS REAL) * 1000.0
            ELSE
              -- assume plain numeric possibly with commas
              CAST(replace(replace(trim(volume), ',', ''), ' ', '') AS REAL)
          END
        )
    END AS volume_num
  FROM bitcoin_prices
), filtered AS (
  -- filter to date range 2021-08-01 through 2021-08-10 inclusive
  SELECT ticker, iso_date AS date, volume_num AS volume
  FROM parsed
  WHERE iso_date BETWEEN '2021-08-01' AND '2021-08-10'
), prev_non_zero AS (
  -- for each row find the most recent prior date for same ticker with volume > 0
  SELECT
    f.ticker,
    f.date,
    f.volume,
    (
      SELECT p.volume
      FROM filtered p
      WHERE p.ticker = f.ticker
        AND p.date < f.date
        AND p.volume > 0
      ORDER BY p.date DESC
      LIMIT 1
    ) AS previous_non_zero_volume
  FROM filtered f
)
SELECT
  ticker,
  date,
  volume,
  previous_non_zero_volume,
  ( (volume - previous_non_zero_volume) / previous_non_zero_volume ) * 100.0 AS percent_change_volume
FROM prev_non_zero
WHERE previous_non_zero_volume IS NOT NULL
  AND previous_non_zero_volume > 0
ORDER BY ticker ASC, date ASC

rows.question: For veg whsle data, can you analyze our financial performance over the years 2020 to 2023? I need insights into the average wholesale price, maximum wholesale price, minimum wholesale price, wholesale price difference, total wholesale price, total selling price, average loss rate, total loss, and profit for each category within each year. Round all calculated values to two decimal places.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH whsle AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(strftime('%Y', whsle_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
    item_code,
    "whsle_px_rmb-kg" AS whsle_px
  FROM veg_whsle_df
  WHERE whsle_date IS NOT NULL
),
txns AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
    item_code,
    "qty_sold(kg)" AS qty_kg,
    "unit_selling_px_rmb/kg" AS sell_px
  FROM veg_txn_df
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
),
cats AS (
  SELECT
    item_code,
    category_name
  FROM veg_cat
),
loss AS (
  SELECT
    l.item_code,
    l."loss_rate_%" AS loss_rate
  FROM veg_loss_rate_df l
),
-- aggregate wholesale stats per year + category
whsle_cat_aggr AS (
  SELECT
    w.year,
    c.category_name AS category,
    AVG(w.whsle_px) AS avg_wholesale,
    MAX(w.whsle_px) AS max_wholesale,
    MIN(w.whsle_px) AS min_wholesale,
    SUM(w.whsle_px) AS sum_wholesale
  FROM whsle w
  LEFT JOIN cats c ON w.item_code = c.item_code
  GROUP BY w.year, c.category_name
),
-- aggregate selling totals per year + category (value = qty * sell_px)
sell_cat_aggr AS (
  SELECT
    t.year,
    c.category_name AS category,
    SUM(COALESCE(t.qty_kg,0) * COALESCE(t.sell_px,0)) AS total_selling
  FROM txns t
  LEFT JOIN cats c ON t.item_code = c.item_code
  GROUP BY t.year, c.category_name
),
-- average loss rate per year + category (use loss_rate from loss table; if no date, assume applicable across years)
loss_cat_aggr AS (
  SELECT
    c.category_name AS category,
    AVG(l.loss_rate) AS avg_loss_rate
  FROM loss l
  LEFT JOIN cats c ON l.item_code = c.item_code
  GROUP BY c.category_name
)
SELECT
  wca.year AS year,
  COALESCE(wca.category, 'Unknown') AS category,
  ROUND(COALESCE(wca.avg_wholesale, 0), 2) AS average_wholesale_price,
  ROUND(COALESCE(wca.max_wholesale, 0), 2) AS maximum_wholesale_price,
  ROUND(COALESCE(wca.min_wholesale, 0), 2) AS minimum_wholesale_price,
  ROUND(COALESCE(wca.max_wholesale, 0) - COALESCE(wca.min_wholesale, 0), 2) AS wholesale_price_difference,
  ROUND(COALESCE(wca.sum_wholesale, 0), 2) AS total_wholesale_price,
  ROUND(COALESCE(sca.total_selling, 0), 2) AS total_selling_price,
  ROUND(COALESCE(lca.avg_loss_rate, 0), 2) AS average_loss_rate,
  -- total_loss = total_wholesale_price * avg_loss_rate / 100
  ROUND(COALESCE(wca.sum_wholesale, 0) * COALESCE(lca.avg_loss_rate, 0) / 100.0, 2) AS total_loss,
  -- profit = total_selling_price - total_wholesale_price - total_loss
  ROUND(
    COALESCE(sca.total_selling, 0)
    - COALESCE(wca.sum_wholesale, 0)
    - (COALESCE(wca.sum_wholesale, 0) * COALESCE(lca.avg_loss_rate, 0) / 100.0)
  , 2) AS profit
FROM whsle_cat_aggr wca
LEFT JOIN sell_cat_aggr sca
  ON sca.year = wca.year AND (sca.category = wca.category OR (sca.category IS NULL AND wca.category IS NULL))
LEFT JOIN loss_cat_aggr lca
  ON lca.category = wca.category
WHERE wca.year IN (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023)
ORDER BY wca.year ASC, wca.category ASC

rows.question: Analyze the average percentage change in sales between the 12 weeks before and after June 15, 2020, for each attribute type: region, platform, age band, demographic, and customer type. For each attribute type, calculate the average percentage change in sales across all its attribute values. Identify the attribute type with the highest negative impact on sales and provide its average percentage change in sales.

WITH
params AS (
  SELECT
    date('2020-06-15') AS pivot_date,
    date('2020-06-15', '-84 days') AS before_start,  -- 12 weeks prior (12*7=84)
    date('2020-06-15', '-1 day') AS before_end,
    date('2020-06-15') AS after_start,
    date('2020-06-15', '+83 days') AS after_end      -- include pivot day and next 83 days = 84 days total
),
sales_filtered AS (
  SELECT
    cws.*,
    -- try to parse week_date formatted as ISO if available, else try common formats
    COALESCE(
      date(week_date_formatted),
      date(week_date),
      -- attempt to interpret week_date like '31/8/20' -> convert to '20-08-31' by strftime not available; fallback to NULL
      NULL
    ) AS iso_week_date
  FROM cleaned_weekly_sales cws
),
sales_windows AS (
  SELECT
    sf.*,
    p.before_start,
    p.before_end,
    p.after_start,
    p.after_end,
    CASE
      WHEN iso_week_date BETWEEN p.before_start AND p.before_end THEN 'before'
      WHEN iso_week_date BETWEEN p.after_start AND p.after_end THEN 'after'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS window
  FROM sales_filtered sf CROSS JOIN params p
  WHERE iso_week_date IS NOT NULL
    AND iso_week_date BETWEEN (SELECT before_start FROM params) AND (SELECT after_end FROM params)
),
agg_by_attr AS (
  -- compute sales_before and sales_after per attribute value for each attribute type
  SELECT 'region' AS attribute_type, region AS attribute_value,
         SUM(CASE WHEN window='before' THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_before,
         SUM(CASE WHEN window='after'  THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_after
  FROM sales_windows
  WHERE region IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY region
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'platform', platform,
         SUM(CASE WHEN window='before' THEN sales ELSE 0 END),
         SUM(CASE WHEN window='after'  THEN sales ELSE 0 END)
  FROM sales_windows
  WHERE platform IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY platform
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'age band', age_band,
         SUM(CASE WHEN window='before' THEN sales ELSE 0 END),
         SUM(CASE WHEN window='after'  THEN sales ELSE 0 END)
  FROM sales_windows
  WHERE age_band IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY age_band
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'demographic', demographic,
         SUM(CASE WHEN window='before' THEN sales ELSE 0 END),
         SUM(CASE WHEN window='after'  THEN sales ELSE 0 END)
  FROM sales_windows
  WHERE demographic IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY demographic
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'customer type', customer_type,
         SUM(CASE WHEN window='before' THEN sales ELSE 0 END),
         SUM(CASE WHEN window='after'  THEN sales ELSE 0 END)
  FROM sales_windows
  WHERE customer_type IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_type
),
pct_changes AS (
  -- exclude attribute values with sales_before = 0 as requested
  SELECT
    attribute_type,
    attribute_value,
    sales_before,
    sales_after,
    CASE
      WHEN sales_before = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE (CAST(sales_after - sales_before AS REAL) / sales_before) * 100.0
    END AS pct_change
  FROM agg_by_attr
),
avg_pct_by_type AS (
  SELECT
    attribute_type,
    AVG(pct_change) AS average_percentage_change_in_sales
  FROM pct_changes
  WHERE pct_change IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY attribute_type
),
max_negative AS (
  -- find the attribute_type with the most negative (smallest) average percentage change
  SELECT attribute_type AS attribute_type_with_highest_negative_impact,
         average_percentage_change_in_sales AS highest_negative_average_percentage_change_in_sales
  FROM avg_pct_by_type
  ORDER BY average_percentage_change_in_sales ASC
  LIMIT 1
)
-- final output: for each attribute_type its average, plus the single worst attribute_type and its value repeated for clarity

  a.average_percentage_change_in_sales,
  m.attribute_type_with_highest_negative_impact,
  m.highest_negative_average_percentage_change_in_sales
FROM avg_pct_by_type a

    SUM(o_inner.total_amt_usd) AS rep_total
  FROM web_orders o_inner
  JOIN web_accounts a_inner ON o_inner.account_id = a_inner.id
  JOIN web_sales_reps sr_inner ON a_inner.sales_rep_id = sr_inner.id
  JOIN web_region r_inner ON sr_inner.region_id = r_inner.id
  GROUP BY r_inner.id, sr_inner.id
) rep_sales ON rep_sales.rep_id = sr.id AND rep_sales.region_id = r.id
JOIN (
  SELECT
    region_id,
    MAX(rep_total) AS max_rep_total
  FROM (
    SELECT
      sr_inner.id AS rep_id,
      r_inner.id AS region_id,
      SUM(o_inner.total_amt_usd) AS rep_total
    FROM web_orders o_inner
    JOIN web_accounts a_inner ON o_inner.account_id = a_inner.id
    JOIN web_sales_reps sr_inner ON a_inner.sales_rep_id = sr_inner.id
    JOIN web_region r_inner ON sr_inner.region_id = r_inner.id
    GROUP BY r_inner.id, sr_inner.id
  )
  GROUP BY region_id
) max_rep ON max_rep.region_id = r.id AND rep_sales.rep_total = max_rep.max_rep_total
GROUP BY r.name, sr.name, rep_sales.rep_total
HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 0
ORDER BY region ASC, top_sales_rep_name ASC

rows.question: Which university faculty members' salaries are closest to the average salary for their respective ranks? Please provide the ranks, first names, last names, and salaries.university
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  f.FacRank AS rank,
  f.FacFirstName AS first_name,
  f.FacLastName AS last_name,
  f.FacSalary AS salary
FROM university_faculty f
JOIN (
  -- compute average salary per rank and minimal distance to that average
  SELECT
    FacRank,
    AVG(FacSalary) AS avg_salary,
    MIN(ABS(FacSalary - AVG(FacSalary))) OVER (PARTITION BY FacRank) AS min_dist
  FROM university_faculty
  WHERE FacSalary IS NOT NULL
    AND FacRank IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY FacRank
) r ON f.FacRank = r.FacRank
WHERE f.FacSalary IS NOT NULL
  AND f.FacRank IS NOT NULL
  AND ABS(f.FacSalary - r.avg_salary) = r.min_dist
ORDER BY f.FacRank ASC

rows.question: Using a Salary Dataset where the salary values need to be cleaned by removing non-numeric characters and converting them to a numeric type, write a detailed SQL query that identifies the top 5 companies by average salary in each of Mumbai, Pune, New Delhi, and Hyderabad, then compares each company’s average salary in those cities to the overall national average salary. The final result should display four columns: Location, Company Name, Average Salary in State, and Average Salary in Country, listing only the top 5 companies in each of the specified locations.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH cleaned AS (
  SELECT
    Location,
    CompanyName,
    -- remove non-digits by chaining replace for common non-digit characters, then cast to numeric
    -- handle possible currency formats like "₹6,48,573/yr" or "6,48,573" or "1191950"
    TRIM(
      REPLACE(
        REPLACE(
          REPLACE(
            REPLACE(
              REPLACE(
                REPLACE(Salary, '₹', ''),
              ',', ''),
            '/yr', ''),
          ' per year', ''),
        '$', ''),
      'USD', '')
    ) AS raw_salary_text,
    -- remove any remaining non-digit characters by removing everything except digits using a simple loop of replaces for common symbols
    NULLIF(
      REPLACE(
        REPLACE(
          REPLACE(
            REPLACE(
              REPLACE(raw_salary_text, ' ', ''),
            '(', ''),
          ')', ''),
        '-', ''),
      '+', '')
    , '') AS cleaned_text
  FROM SalaryDataset
  WHERE Salary IS NOT NULL
),
numeric AS (
  SELECT
    Location,
    CompanyName,
    -- convert cleaned text to numeric. If cleaned_text still contains non-digit characters, try casting; invalid casts become NULL
    CASE
      WHEN cleaned_text GLOB '*[0-9]*' THEN CAST(cleaned_text AS REAL)
      ELSE NULL
    END AS salary_num
  FROM cleaned
),
state_company_avg AS (
  SELECT
    Location,
    CompanyName,
    AVG(salary_num) AS avg_state_salary
  FROM numeric
  WHERE Location IN ('Mumbai','Pune','New Delhi','Hyderabad')
    AND salary_num IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY Location, CompanyName
),
country_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(salary_num) AS avg_country_salary
  FROM numeric
  WHERE salary_num IS NOT NULL
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    sca.Location,
    sca.CompanyName,
    sca.avg_state_salary,
    ca.avg_country_salary,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sca.Location ORDER BY sca.avg_state_salary DESC) AS rn
  FROM state_company_avg sca
  CROSS JOIN country_avg ca
)
SELECT
  Location,
  CompanyName AS "Company Name",
  ROUND(avg_state_salary, 2) AS "Average Salary in State",
  ROUND(avg_country_salary, 2) AS "Average Salary in Country"
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= 5
ORDER BY Location, "Average Salary in State" DESC
